service.description: The in-parameters the People app services share; each service declares what it returns.

Check that the user may open People and resolve their scope and the app's routes: capabilities (the People and payroll permissions, and the areas), the employers a staff reader sees as options and whether they are every one, the units under them, the user's own party and current employments, and the links. Refuses a user without People (PEOPLE_UNAVAILABLE), a Projects client contact, a PASS public account and a self-service employee among them, and another app root (PEOPLE_CONTEXT). Pay values are never part of it.

parameter.name: organizationOptions
parameter.description: The employers as {value, label}, by name, at most 100

service.description: A record a People screen or mount was given: an employer or a person (People.js recordKinds; later phases add theirs). Answers its kind's name, a label and a short detail (a person's employers in the user's scope). Refuses a record that does not exist and one outside the scope alike (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE): an organization that is not an employer the user sees, a person neither self, a live report nor employed by such an employer. With a capability named (hrView, configure, ...), refuses a user without it (PERMISSION_DENIED).

The options of a People drop-down the user may choose, searched by term in the query ignoring case, with the selected value's label: employers (those a staff reader sees), units (the employers and the departments and teams under them), people (the current employees of those employers, the user's live reports and the user with self-service), employees (P3: the current employees of organizationPartyId, else of every employer the user reads, the managers and members OrgStructure and OrgChart choose), departments (P4: the departments of organizationPartyId, a position's), jobClasses (the current job classes) and payGrades (the pay grades by name, never an amount). Refuses a user without People and an unknown choice.

parameter.name: organizationPartyId
parameter.description: employees and departments: the employer whose employees or departments are offered

service.description: The palette's People records, each opening its People screen: the directory (P2), the people mantle.humanres.PeopleServices.find#Employees reaches for the user and the text, each once, as their public work identity, opening Employee360, with recordEntity and recordId. No rows for a user without People.

A person's record as Shared/Employee360 shows it under appRoot (design §4 Employee360's per-app context, crosscut §3.4; People.js employee360Apps): mantle.humanres.PeopleServices.get#Employee360's answer narrowed to the regions the app shows (People every admitted region; Commons the Overview and the user's own personal information; Insights the Overview, read only), the fields the user may change there and the return link. A context narrows and grants nothing. A person outside the user's People scope answers recordFound false; another app root is refused (PEOPLE_CONTEXT), and People's mount needs the People root (PEOPLE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameter.name: record
parameter.description: partyId, overview, personalInfo (when shown), partyRelationshipId, hostEmploymentId (the employment host, when its files and activity are shown)

service.description: Where the user opens a person's record from an app with no Employee360 context (Projects' PersonDetail, Admin's UserDetail): People/Employees/Employee360 for a People user whose scope admits the person as staff or team, Commons/People/Employee360 for one it admits otherwise (the person themselves), else no url. The link adds no right; Employee360 checks again.

People's record-lookup provider (People.xml shell-providers, people.records; design §1.4 Comms hooks): the Person over the directory projection. search: the people find#Employees reaches for text, as optionList of {value: mantle.party.Party|id, label}; info and card: a person the user's People scope admits, as their public work identity, with their Employee360 link (a person it does not admit is left out, so another provider answers for them); links: the people a message's Employee360 links name, up to five.
